qualifying_findings.summary: SuperAGI through v0.0.14 lets an authenticated user from one organization retrieve another organization's agent inventory by supplying its project_id; the controller does not verify project ownership.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: SuperAGI through v0.0.14; /api/agents/get/project/{project_id} cross-tenant controller boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An agent inventory exposes delegated capabilities and organization-specific automation context, so tenant-scoped authorization must bind each agent query to the caller's organization.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: SuperAGI product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local multi-tenant agent authorization implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Confirm a maintainer patch or fixed release and inventory exposed multi-tenant SuperAGI deployments before synthesis.

qualifying_findings.summary: SuperAGI v0.0.14 permits an authenticated attacker from one organization to obtain another organization's latest agent execution and metadata through a victim project_id.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Execution metadata can reveal agent behavior and operational context; authorization must be checked before retrieving project-scoped agent state.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: SuperAGI product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local agent-execution isolation implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Reconcile this separately from CVE-2026-51902 because the protected resource is execution state rather than agent inventory.

qualifying_findings.summary: SuperAGI v0.0.14 lacks an organization ownership check when returning agent execution configuration, allowing an authenticated cross-tenant caller to read a victim agent_id and agent_execution_id pair.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent execution configuration may encode tool, model, credential-reference, and workflow choices, making it sensitive cross-tenant control-plane data.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: SuperAGI product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local agent configuration confidentiality and authorization implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Confirm fixed versions and assess whether configuration responses contain credential material or sensitive tool endpoints.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE API public record with public upstream issue reference
qualifying_findings.summary: OpenBMB XAgent v1.0.0 contains a directory-traversal flaw in ToolServerNode's upload_file handler, allowing a file-upload name to escape the intended working directory.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: OpenBMB XAgent v1.0.0; ToolServer/ToolServerNode/main.py upload_file at the agent tool-server filesystem boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent-accessible tool servers convert untrusted contextual input into host file operations; path containment must be enforced after normalization.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: XAgent product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local agent-tool filesystem-containment implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Verify a maintainer remediation and keep upload-capable tool servers sandboxed until a fixed version is established.

qualifying_findings.summary: modelscope agent-zero versions 1.7 through 1.10 accept a user-controlled path in FileBrowser.save_text_file without normalization or validation, enabling directory traversal.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent file-browser functions are delegated write authority; user- or prompt-derived paths need canonical containment checks before host file creation.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: agent-zero product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local delegated filesystem-write control implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Locate a maintainer advisory or release fix and review deployments for writable paths beyond the intended workspace.

confidence_notes: All retained findings have precise October 29 NVD publication timestamps inside the cutoff window and are directly reproducible through the public NVD CVE API.

The three SuperAGI CVEs share a product but protect independently changing tenant-scoped resources: agent inventory, execution metadata, and execution configuration; preserve that separation during ingestion.
NVD-first evidence does not establish a fixed release for the retained entries; maintainer advisories and remediation status require ingest-time confirmation.
No docs/wiki or raw/processed content was changed by this collection run.
